parsed.notes: No quote-fidelity or pincite assertion rows were present in group_inventory.jsonl, so this review covers the five disclosed rows exactly once.

reasons: The lake identity record is non-stub and names Go-Bart Importing Co. v. United States with U.S. Supreme Court as the court and 1931 as the year.
The official, parallel, and vendor-neutral citations in the assertion match the lake citation fields.

defect.evidence_quote: No question is here raised as to the search of the persons.
defect.problem: The case is foundational for limiting search incident to arrest as to premises/general exploratory searches, but the disclosed opinion expressly says the search of persons was not at issue, making the home label 'SIA Persons' over-specific unless the page is intended to cover SITA generally.
defect.proposed_fix: Retain the case as historical/foundational only on a general SITA scope or premises/general-search page, or relabel the role as a historical SITA boundary case not a person-search authority.

reasons: The opinion treats the remaining issue as the search of the premises and papers, not the arrestees' persons.
The lake treatment scope note supports a foundational SITA limit, but not a person-search-specific holding.
residual_risks: If 'SIA Persons' is an internal page name for all search-incident-to-arrest doctrine, the defect is naming/placement rather than substantive support.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Clarify that Go-Bart is a historical SITA scope/premises case, not authority about searching the arrestee's person.

reasons: The text supports the fact-specific reasonableness component and states that the office search was an unreasonable search of the premises.
The text supports the general-exploratory-search characterization and distinguishes a permissible Marron incident search from the broader office rummaging here.
The assertion does not materially overclaim so long as it is read as a premises/general-search limit, not a person-search rule.
residual_risks: The word 'warrantless' compresses the procedural posture; the agents acted under color of an invalid warrant, while the Court assumed the arrests lawful without relying on that warrant.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Consider saying 'assuming the arrests lawful, the agents could not use them to justify ransacking the office for evidence.'

reasons: Treatment is outside lens A's substantive charter; the asserted treatment fields match the disclosed lake treatment fields.
The lake record provides field_i_validity, dates, composite basis, varies_by_point, and the same scope note.
residual_risks: No independent treatment/currency audit was performed under lens A.

reasons: The lake identity record classifies the court as U.S. Supreme Court with court_level scotus.
In this federal corpus, the page's 'Binding — SCOTUS' label is supported by the disclosed court identity.
residual_risks: This verifies weight from disclosed court identity only, not any separate treatment/currency question.
